instruction:
Read docs/TASK_PHASE16.md FIRST: sections 2.3 (tests/setup.ts and tests/helpers.ts: every signature there is the contract), 2.4, 3.1 and 4; then in contour.yaml the Requirement Frontend Tree and, in group dashboard-ui, the Function descriptions (the module layout) and Merge Feed example 5 (the UPGRADE event). The four fixtures are in your context.

You write the scaffold of dashboard/, a Node project of its own inside a Python repository, six files and nothing else:
- dashboard/package.json: name "ethsc-dashboard", private true, type "module", scripts {"build": "vite build", "test": "vitest run"}, no dependencies, devDependencies exactly {"@types/node": "22.20.5", "happy-dom": "20.14.5", "typescript": "5.9.3", "vite": "7.3.6", "vitest": "3.2.7"} (exact versions, no ^ or ~).
- dashboard/tsconfig.json: strict true, noEmit true, target and lib ES2022 plus DOM and DOM.Iterable, module ESNext, moduleResolution bundler, types ["vite/client", "node"], skipLibCheck true, include ["src", "tests"].
- dashboard/vite.config.ts: defineConfig from "vitest/config"; build {outDir "dist", sourcemap false, emptyOutDir true}; test {environment "happy-dom", include ["tests/**/*.test.ts"], setupFiles ["tests/setup.ts"], chaiConfig {truncateThreshold 200}}. No public directory.
- dashboard/index.html: a minimal HTML5 page titled "ethsc dashboard" with <div id="app"> and <script type="module" src="/src/main.ts"></script> (src/ is written by later cards).
- dashboard/tests/setup.ts: replaces globalThis.fetch, XMLHttpRequest and WebSocket, and the connect and createConnection of the default export of "node:net", with functions that throw Error("network blocked in tests"); a test that needs fetch passes a fake from helpers.
- dashboard/tests/helpers.ts: exactly the exports of section 2.3, behaving as written there. Read the fixtures with node:fs at path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "../../tests/fixtures/dashboard_<name>.json") (fileURLToPath from node:url, given the string import.meta.url; never new URL(...): under happy-dom the global URL is not Node's and node:fs refuses it); FixtureEvent is declared here (helpers imports nothing from src/). fixtureEvents and syntheticEvents return fresh objects every call; syntheticEvents copies the fixture event with id 8 and sets id and block to each i.

You write TypeScript for dashboard/, a Node project of its own inside a Python repository (package.json, tsconfig.json and vite.config.ts are in dashboard/; every command runs there). TypeScript strict, ESM imports with relative paths and no file extension ("./api"), no `any` (use `unknown` and narrow). 

Write no test file: the scaffold is checked by a probe. Do not write package-lock.json: the acceptance runs npm install, which writes it.
